name: Dr. Memory
workload: Memory-error checking of SPEC CPU2006 on Linux; slowdown versus native for Dr. Memory and Valgrind.
claimed_speedup: README: 'faster than comparable tools, including Valgrind' on SPECCPU 2006 (chart only, no numbers in the README text; Valgrind cannot run 434.zeusmp and 447.dealII)
tradeoffs: Built on DynamoRIO; Windows, Linux, Mac, Android. Different checks than Memcheck, not a drop-in clone.
caveats: Numbers are in a bar chart image and in the CGO 2011 paper (peer reviewed), which is on a blocked host (burningcutlery.com) so not read; 2011 results on old Valgrind. No flags or CPU model seen, so tier B not A.
found_via: WebSearch: github dynamic binary instrumentation faster than Valgrind memcheck; HN item 'Dr. Memory: A Memory Checker Faster Than Valgrind'; opened README

name: heaptrack
workload: Heap allocation profiling of applications; overhead in time and memory versus Massif.
claimed_speedup: Qualitative only: overhead in both time and memory 'significantly lower'; multi-threaded programs are not serialized; CPU-bound code between allocations is not slowed at all
tradeoffs: Linux only; Massif handles pool allocators and stack allocation better (README says so); trace files can be large.
caveats: No numbers in the README. License is in a LICENSES directory and was not read, so usability left conservative; likely LGPL-2.1-or-later (not confirmed). Third-party reports of OOM on very large runs.
found_via: WebSearch: heaptrack OR bytehound OR memray heap profiler faster than valgrind massif overhead; opened repo and README

name: funtrace
workload: Per-call overhead of instrumented function entry and return in a microbenchmark; also compared with LLVM XRay.
claimed_speedup: <10 ns per instrumented call or return; 6x faster than LLVM XRay flight recorder mode, 15-18x faster than XRay basic logging, 4.5x faster than uftrace
compiler_and_flags: gcc and clang with -finstrument-functions, gcc -pg -mfentry, or clang -fxray-instrument (flags for the benchmark build not stated)
tradeoffs: x86-64 Linux only; needs compiler instrumentation and a recompile; tracing profiler, not a sampler, so it is a different workflow than perf; trace buffer is a ring and snapshots pause tracing.
caveats: Own microbenchmark, hardware not stated; author notes uftrace targets a different workflow. Baseline is uftrace and XRay, not perf, gprof or Valgrind.
found_via: WebSearch: github uftrace OR function tracer overhead compared gprof -pg -finstrument-functions benchmark faster

name: MicroProfiler (micro-profiler)
workload: Profiling overhead on 7-Zip across profilers, shown as an image in the README.
claimed_speedup: README graphic 'profiled 7-Zip performance' shows lower overhead than gprof, Valgrind and VTune; no numeric values in the README text. Changelog: up to 35% (x86) and 42% (x64) less profiler overhead than its own previous version.
tradeoffs: Instrumentation (compiler hook) profiler, needs recompilation; Visual Studio integration; Windows and Linux.
caveats: Comparison is an image whose numbers I could not read; graphic only seen by link, not opened. First-party only.
found_via: WebSearch: github C++ instrumentation profiler ns per scope overhead benchmark; opened repo and README

name: DoubleTake
workload: Detecting heap buffer overflows, use-after-free and leaks via evidence-based rollback and replay; runtime overhead.
claimed_speedup: README: 'just 2% overhead on average' when detecting buffer overflows only; paper (arXiv 1601.07962) says significantly more efficient than prior dynamic tools with under 5% overhead
tradeoffs: Detects errors after the fact and replays; limited to a subset of what Memcheck finds; Linux research prototype.
caveats: No Valgrind numbers on the README page; paper (blocked here, snippet only) is a peer-reviewed PLDI-class result but head-to-head figures were not read. Abandoned since 2016.
found_via: WebSearch: github dynamic binary instrumentation faster than Valgrind memcheck; DoubleTake arXiv result

name: memtrail
workload: LD_PRELOAD memory profiler and leak detector for long-running CPU-heavy workloads.
claimed_speedup: Qualitative: 'very little runtime overhead'; built because workloads 'run too slow under Valgrind'
tradeoffs: Linux LD_PRELOAD only; less detailed than Valgrind.
caveats: No numbers; repo has benchmark.cpp but no results were read. License not found on the page. Tier D with 89 stars is below the notability bar; kept per keep-and-document rule for the orchestrator to decide.
found_via: WebSearch: github DrCCTProf OR memory profiler OR leak detector overhead Valgrind

name: heapusage
workload: LD_PRELOAD heap error and leak finder, a small subset of Memcheck functionality.
claimed_speedup: Qualitative: 'less performance impact than Valgrind'; for large applications that cannot run at Valgrind slowdown
tradeoffs: Less precise than Memcheck; Linux and macOS.
caveats: No numbers anywhere in the README.
